headline: Commodities Retreat Sharply as Metals and Crude Face Broad Pressure
paragraphs: Copper led today's market declines, falling 5.52% to 5.15 euros per pound amid unwinding AI trades, Chinese demand concerns, and a firmer US dollar. Silver tumbled 5.31% to 40.86 euros per ounce, pressured by greenback strength and a hawkish Federal Reserve tone. Bucking the wider commodity downturn, natural gas rallied 5.24% to 3.08 euros per MMBtu on forecasts of colder US weather.

Platinum dropped 5.08% to 1,235.34 euros per ounce amid cautious spot market sentiment, though specific drivers beyond the wider metals sell-off remain unclear. Crude oil retreated sharply as WTI fell 4.84% to 74.69 euros per barrel and Brent lost 4.49% to 81.18 euros per barrel, weighed down by higher US crude stocks and expectations of a global supply surplus. Gold sank 3.95% to 3,386.93 euros per ounce as the stronger US dollar dampened market sentiment. Finally, palladium fell 2.93% to 863.23 euros per ounce, with distinct individual catalysts also unclear.
